question: Which part of the body do doctors check using a proctoscopy?
explanation: You've got this! A proctoscopy focuses right on the lower end of the digestive tract, which is the rectum and anal canal. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is a very common reason a doctor orders a proctoscopy for a patient with bright red blood in their stool?
explanation: Spot on! Hemorrhoids are one of the most frequent causes of bright red rectal bleeding that doctors investigate with a proctoscopy. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of severe anal pain and bright red blood after passing stool. What test will the doctor likely do first?
explanation: Well done! When symptoms happen right at the end of the digestive tract, a proctoscopy is the quickest and most direct way to see what's going on. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main job of the rounded obturator inside a rigid proctoscope?

options.A: To magnify small polyps for better visual inspection
options.B: To deliver continuous oxygen to the lower bowel wall
options.C: To prevent trauma to the mucosal lining during insertion
options.D: To suction out liquid stool and blood from the field

explanation: Think of the obturator as a smooth shield. Its rounded tip helps guide the scope safely past the tight anal muscles without scratching the delicate tissue inside. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why must a nurse always make sure a water-soluble lubricant is used for a proctoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the light source from overheating inside the rectum
options.B: To sterilize the metal components of privacy equipment instantly
options.C: To act as a strong local anesthetic agent for the rectal walls
options.D: To ease smooth passage through the anal sphincter without harming tissue

explanation: Great choice! Water-soluble jelly reduces friction so the scope slides in comfortably without hurting the patient, and it washes away easily afterward. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h3)

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?
explanation: Spot on! Because a proctoscopy only looks at the very end of the bowel, a quick cleansing enema just before the test is usually all it takes to clear the area. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why do we ask a patient to empty their bladder right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: To activate systemic blood pressure medications
options.B: To reduce pelvic pressure and enhance comfort
options.C: To prevent sudden urinary tract infections
options.D: To collect a routine clean-catch urine specimen

explanation: That's correct! An empty bladder takes up less room in the pelvis, which leaves more space and makes the exam much more comfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which patient position is most commonly used for a routine proctoscopy?
explanation: You got it! The left lateral (or Sims') position is the standard, most comfortable posture for a patient during this exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient suddenly feels dizzy, sweaty, and pale during a proctoscopy. What should you, as the nurse, do immediately?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Administer an oral laxative to clear remaining stool
options.C: Encourage the patient to push harder to finish the test
options.D: Stop the procedure immediately and notify the clinician

explanation: Safety first! These are classic signs of a vasovagal faint. Always pause the procedure right away and get help to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why might a patient feel like they need to pass gas right after having a proctoscopy?

options.A: The enema fluid causes permanent irritation of the bowel
options.B: Dietary restrictions create excess gas in the stomach
options.C: Air is introduced into the rectum during the examination
options.D: Local anesthetics paralyze the internal sphincter muscles

explanation: That's right! The doctor pumps a little air into the bowel to see clearly, which naturally leaves the patient feeling a bit full or gassy afterward. It passes quickly! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is an important warning sign you must teach a patient before they go home after a proctoscopy?

options.C: Mild passing of gas for two hours
options.D: A temporary feeling of rectal fullness

explanation: Spot on! A tiny bit of spotting can happen, but heavy or ongoing bleeding is not normal. Always tell patients to report this right away. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h6)
